thread:
incident-bot: Incident created · Severity P1 · kv-cache eviction rate spike in prod (region us-west-2). Auto-alert: cache_pressure > 85% for 5m :rotating_light:
Sanjay: I'm on it, linking traces now. seeing a sudden jump in kv cache entries across awq models, KV size per-request up ~3x compared to baseline.
Robert: any deploys in the last hour?
Sanjay: no user-facing deploys. infra autoscaler did a node add ~10m ago.
Elle: running top queries on the runtime nodes — continuous-batcher queues are growing, avg batch size shot from 6 -> 22.
Kevin: that explains footprint. If batcher packs many long-context requests with AWQ int8 kernels, kvs blow past our eviction thresholds.
Nadia: is this only AWQ or also gptq paths? I saw a related alert earlier for gptq-24b but it was quieter.
Sanjay: telemetry shows the quant path selector favored awq-int8_fma kernel on these nodes; the kernel returns 3x per-token kv bytes compared to the normal int8 path.
Robert: customer impact? Are we dropping requests or just higher latency?
Elle: a subset of customers hitting long-chat flows are seeing throttles + higher latencies; some sessions hit paging and get 502s when KV eviction can't catch up.
ops-bot: PagerDuty incident: assigned to oncall-runtime (Sanjay). Severity changed to P1.
Sanjay: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) reduce continuous-batcher max_batch_size and max_batch_wait to limit aggregate KV growth 2) enable kernel fallback to the safe int8 kernel for awq models 3) route heavy-context customers to a dedicated pool with higher kv limits.
Kevin: I can roll the batcher throttles now. Patch:
```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_size: 24 -> 10
  max_batch_wait_ms: 50 -> 20
  max_concurrent_batches: 12 -> 6
```
Kevin: applying to canary pool first.
Nadia: I'll push kernel-fallback flag (runtime config) to true so the selector can prefer smaller-kv kernels under pressure.
Sanjay: add a temporary quota increase for the dedicated pool and route top 5 affected customers there. I'll DM @sales for consent where needed.
Robert: notify support to prepare customer comms for affected accounts; mark as potential 5–10% error-rate bump last 30m.
Elle: quick check on retention: top offending model is "open-awq-13b-v2" with median context 3k tokens for the requests in the window.
Sanjay: executing mitigation steps in order: 1) Kevin change -> canary applied 2145678950, monitoring 2) Nadia toggle -> 2145679012 3) route config -> 2145679065
Kevin: canary observation: batch size distribution dropped, kv pressure down ~40% on canary nodes within 60s.
Nadia: kernel-fallback toggle worked, selector logs show fallback path for ~32% of awq sessions.
Sanjay: routing pushed — two heavy customers moved to dedicated pool, their tail latencies stabilized.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: config-change applied to canary (change-id: cfg-9872).
Elle: still seeing eviction events but rate is decreasing. Paging events down from 120/min -> 28/min on the impacted cluster.
Robert: what's the plan for permanent fix?
Sanjay: short-term: keep batcher throttle + kernel-fallback + routing. Medium-term: adjust kernel selection heuristics to include kv-footprint estimate, instrument per-kernel kv bytes in model metadata, and add a batching budget that considers KV costs not just tokens.
Nadia: I can prototype a kernel-scoring patch to penalize high-kv kernels when cache_util > 60%.
Kevin: we'll also add an autoscale guard to avoid adding back nodes that cause more aggregate kv (the autoscaler was counterproductive earlier).
Robert: make a timeline for rollback to defaults: only after 48h of stable metrics and no customer escalations.
Sanjay: customer-impact summary for postmortem: ~8 customers experienced elevated latency; 2 customers saw intermittent 502s for long-chat flows. No data loss. Estimated cost increase from routing to dedicated pool ~+$2.1k for the incident window.
Elle: collecting logs and sample sessions for the postmortem, adding perf diffs for awq-int8_fma vs safe-int8.
ops-bot: Handoff reminder: oncall rotation change in 2h. SRE oncall (Robert) will take watch after SRE warm-handoff.
Robert: I'll keep monitoring and lead the postmortem write-up. Sanjay, leave the kernel-fallback enabled until we push a selector patch.
Sanjay: agreed. I'll also open a follow-up ticket to add per-model kv estimates in the model registry.
Nadia: FYI, opened GH issue: redwood/runtime#1423 — 'kernel kv-byte metadata' with proposed schema.
Sanjay: good. Logging summary:
```text
- Root cause: kernel selector favored a high-kv AWQ kernel under recent workload distribution
- Immediate mitigations: batcher throttles, kernel-fallback toggle, customer routing
- Impact: latency increase and paging-induced 502s for long-context sessions, 8 customers affected
- Next actions: kernel scoring, kv metadata, autoscaler guard, telemetry alert tuning
```
Robert: thanks all. We'll convert this thread into the incident postmortem channel once we have full logs. :white_check_mark:
